title: Walden and Other Writings

vibeProfile.oneLine: Thoreau's classic of simple living by Walden Pond, plus Civil Disobedience.

summary: Henry David Thoreau's account of the two years he spent living simply in a cabin by Walden Pond is the founding text of American nature writing and a timeless argument for a deliberate, unhurried life close to the natural world. Gathered here with other essays including 'Civil Disobedience', his influential defence of conscience against the state, it distils a whole philosophy of self-reliance and attention. Reflective, quotable and quietly radical, it still speaks to anyone seeking a simpler, more mindful way to live.
whyReadIt: The founding book of nature writing and simple living, with 'Civil Disobedience' alongside. Quietly radical and endlessly quoted.

funFacts.text: His essay 'Civil Disobedience' later influenced Gandhi and Martin Luther King.
